s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic facial swelling with reduced mouth opening and prior similar episodes
salient_findings: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
Reduced mouth opening
Gross right facial asymmetry
Ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders
Elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa
key_facts: First episode treated as buccal-space infection with incision and drainage
Swelling extended from the level of the right lateral canthus to 1 cm below the corner of the mouth
Swelling extended from the corner of the mouth posteriorly to the mandibular ramus
Elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas
Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content
Erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla

shortlist.label: Actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, recurrent facial swelling with ill-defined borders and cystic areas on CT

shortlist.label: Buccal mucosa carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic facial swelling with elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa

shortlist.label: Minor salivary gland tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous swelling in the buccal space with restricted mouth opening

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas and leathery pouch-like appearance

shortlist.label: Branchial cleft cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, asymptomatic facial swelling with normal overlying skin and ill-defined borders

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas, intracystic loculations, and a leathery pouch-like appearance of the excised specimen are consistent with a dermoid cyst. The lack of pain, fever, or lymphadenopathy also supports this diagnosis, as dermoid cysts are typically benign and asymptomatic.

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: Actinomycosis is typically associated with pain, fever, and lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Buccal mucosa carcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of vestibular obliteration, paresthesia, or facial palsy makes carcinoma less likely.

rejected.label: Minor salivary gland tumor
rejected.why: The location and appearance of the mass are not typical for a minor salivary gland tumor.

rejected.label: Branchial cleft cyst
rejected.why: The location of the mass in the buccal space, rather than in the neck, makes branchial cleft cyst less likely.
